answer: Detection is outsourced to a bounty market. Every submission is registered, and any observer earns a reward for proving two records share one operator: identical text, a reused key, or a slot matched to the second. Payouts come from staked balances, so every clone raises the cost of hiding. A claim may cite only settled epochs, never past a fixed horizon, blocking cherry-picked evidence. Honest histories harden into a crystal of fixed facets, so imitators must copy the evidence itself. One report traces a plume of shared fingerprints across the cluster. Collusion costs more than answering.
